agent: wave brief G - the alignment triangle, start to drift
question: Where a country's alignment position starts in a new game, when the drift runs, the two unread globals and gates of the seven terms, the clamp, and whether one drift step reproduces the saves.

addresses.name: CAlignment::CAlignment
addresses.comment: 0x4C3050 to the `ret 4` at 0x4C3123, the object on the stack. vftable 0x15C0CC0, CPersistent type id 0x18D at +4, then **every dword from +8 to +0x44 zeroed** - position, centroid, the weight vector's three pointers and the eight bounds dwords - the ideology database built if it is not yet (0x5272E0/0x528220), the weight vector sized to the group count (0x4C4E80, a vector<int> resize), and ClampMove called with a zero move, which is there for its side effect: it builds the bounds (+0x28..+0x44) once. So a new CAlignment sits at (0, 0) until the history or a save says otherwise. Called from CCountry::CCountry at 0x4C8BA8 with country + 0xDC.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end; the call site is `lea ecx,[ebx+0xdc]; push ecx; call 0x4c3050` at 0x4C8B9B. Wrong if a second caller passes something that is not a CCountry's +0xDC.

addresses.name: CAlignment::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2. Writes `position = { x y }` - token 0x4B, the point at this + 8 - through the point writer 0xA7A080 (token in ecx, writer in eax, the point pushed). The whole of what a save keeps of a CAlignment: no weights, no bounds, no centroid. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Seven instructions, 0x4C31E0..0x4C31F5; vtable.py --holding puts it in CAlignment slot 2 alone. The saves carry exactly `alignment = { position = { x y } }` per country, three decimals.

addresses.name: CAlignment::RebuildBounds
addresses.comment: Builds the triangle the political compass is clamped to, **once**: it does nothing unless the width (+0x30) and height (+0x34) are both still 0. The box starts as the zero-size box at (+0x28, +0x2C) - which the constructor zeroed, so **it always contains the origin** - and grows to take in every ideology group's position (+0x58/+0x5C of each entry of the database at 0x1A878BC, +0x1C..+0x20): +0x28 min x, +0x2C min y, +0x30 width, +0x34 height. Then, thousandths, every divide truncating: mid = minX + width - width*1000/2000; +0x3C = -height*1000 / (mid - minX) and +0x38 = -height*1000 / (mid - (minX + width)) - the slopes of the triangle's two edges from an apex at the **bottom middle** of the box (-1 where a divisor is 0) - and +0x40 = +0x44 = min y, the apex's y. With Their Finest Hour's three groups (200,200), (0,-146), (-200,200): the box -200..200 x -146..200, slopes -1730 and +1730, apex y -146000. Called by ClampMove and ClampPosition only.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end; two callers (0x4C49FB, 0x4C4B1D), both `mov edi, esi` first. The slopes reproduce the USA's start: its history x 20 is pulled to 9.788 = (−129.066 + 146) x 1000 / 1730, the edge at its new y, to the thousandth.

addresses.name: CAlignment::UpdateCentroid
addresses.comment: +0x10 = (minX + (minX + width) + mid) / 3 and +0x14 = (minY + 2 x (minY + height)) / 3 - the centroid of the bounds triangle (0, 84.667 in Their Finest Hour), computed after every clamp. **No reader of +0x10/+0x14 was found** in the clamp, the drift or the terms; what uses it is not established.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end; four callers, all tail calls of ClampMove (0x4C4CA2, 0x4C4CBB) and ClampPosition (0x4C4ADF, 0x4C4AF2). The arithmetic is (2*minX + width + mid)*1000/3000 and (3*minY + 2*height)*1000/3000.

addresses.name: CAlignment::ClampPosition
addresses.comment: Clamps the position itself, not a move: x into [minX, minX + width], y into [minY, minY + height], then x between the triangle's two edges at that y - left = (y - apexY) x 1000 / leftSlope, right = (y - apexY) x 1000 / rightSlope, **both measured from x = 0**, so the code assumes the apex is at x 0. Unlike ClampMove it has no sign slip. One caller: CCgmAlignmentChangeCommand::Execute, the custom game's alignment slider - outside the canonical start.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end; findRefs --callers 0x4C49F0 gives the one site 0x429BA4.

addresses.name: CAlignment::ClampMove
addresses.signature: Point* __fastcall CAlignment::ClampMove(CAlignment* this@EAX, Point* out@stack:4, Point* delta@stack:8) @EAX
addresses.comment: `ret 8`, `this` in EAX. out = delta; RebuildBounds (once); then, with every test made against the **unchanged** delta: if pos.x + delta.x > minX + width, out.x = minX + width - pos.x; if pos.x + delta.x < minX, **out.x = pos.x - minX** (the sign is the wrong way round - the bytes are `mov eax,[esi+8]; sub eax, minX`); if pos.y + delta.y > minY + height, out.y = minY + height - pos.y; if below minY, out.y = minY - pos.y. Then the triangle, at the new y = pos.y + out.y: left = (y - apexY) x 1000 / leftSlope, right = (y - apexY) x 1000 / rightSlope, both from x = 0; new x = pos.x + out.x; if new x < left, out.x = left - pos.x, else if new x > right, out.x = right - pos.x. UpdateCentroid last. In Their Finest Hour the sign slip is masked: anything left of x -200 is also left of the left edge, and the triangle step overwrites out.x. Called by the constructor (a zero move, to build the bounds) and by CAlignment::UpdateDaily. **This is what puts a history position that lies outside the triangle back on it** - USA's and CAN's 20,-128.7 both land on the right edge on day one.
addresses.revises: Was `likely`, saying only that it shortens the move to stay in the bounding box. Read end to end: it clamps to the triangle, not the box, the x-below-minimum arm has its sign reversed, and the signature now places both stack arguments.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x4C4B00..0x4C4CC8 in full (both `ret 8`). Positive check against the saves: the start save's USA (9.788, -129.066) and CAN (9.734, -129.160) are exactly the right edge at their new y, from history x 20.

addresses.name: CAlignment::GetRevanchismTerm
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall CAlignment::GetRevanchismTerm(int* out, CIdeologyGroup* group, CCountry* country)
addresses.comment: Subtracted by the aggregator, and only for a country in no faction. s = CFaction::GetVictoryPointShare(group's faction) x 1000 / 100000 - the faction's share of the world's victory points in thousandths. **When s >= 500, zero.** Otherwise per = (1000 - s) x 5000 / 1000 - **five times (1 - s), not (0.5 - s)**: the bytes are `sub esi, eax` (esi = s - 500, `jns` to the zero arm) and then `sub eax, esi` with eax = 500, i.e. 500 - (s - 500). total = per x (number of the country's cores, CCountry +0xD10, whose province's owner (+0x330) is not the country and whose owner's faction (+0xD8) **is** the group's faction - the null faction included, for a group with none). Then total x REVANCHISM_WEIGHT (alignment +0x10) / 1000 x (1000 + SUSEPTIBILITY) / 1000 x (1000 + suseptibility_<faction>) / 1000. So the weight per core falls from 0.5 at s = 0 to 0.25 just under s = 0.5 and then **drops to nothing**. The 500 is floor(500.50003f), the float at 0x160A5E8.
addresses.revises: The record had (0.5 - s) x 5; the bytes compute (1 - s) x 5 below the 0.5 cut-off. Corrected from 0x4C3FCE..0x4C3FF0, and the core loop, the null-faction case and the order of the three scalings are now stated.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x4C3F45..0x4C4100. The start save confirms the size: IND's 276 cores held by the allies, ENG's 275 and FRA's one, give its day-one move of 68 units only at 5.0 per core x 0.1, i.e. (1 - s) x 5 with s = 0; (0.5 - s) x 5 gives half and misses by 15 units. PAK, IRE, TIB and GUY agree the same way.

addresses.name: CAlignment::GetAlignTowardsTerm
addresses.signature: int* __fastcall CAlignment::GetAlignTowardsTerm(int* out@stack:4, CCountry* country@stack:8, CIdeologyGroup* group@EDI) @EAX
addresses.comment: `ret 8` and the group arrives in **edi**. The term the game's tooltip calls FACTION_DRIFT_INFLUENCE. Zero unless the country is in no faction, the group's faction has members, and the country **has the static modifier its faction's `influence` string names** (`align_towards_axis` and the rest, found by name through 0x523560 and tested with CountryHasModifier). Then, thousandths, truncating: v = that modifier's own ALIGN_TOWARDS value (values entry 47, +0x178; 20.000 for all three in Their Finest Hour's static_modifiers.txt); a = (100000 - max(leader's EffectiveNeutrality, 0)) x 1000 / 100000; b = (100000 - country's EffectiveNeutrality) x 1000 / 100000 + 250, **floored at 250**; out = b x (a x v / 1000) / 1000. The 250 is [0x1A87334]'s neighbour [0x1A8732C], floor(250.5f), set by InitAlignmentInfluenceFloor - so a fully neutral country still feels a quarter of the pull. The leader is the faction's first member.
addresses.revises: The global [0x1A8732C] is now known (250, a .CRT$XCU initialiser), and the floor on the country's factor, the leader being the first member, the modifier test and the order of the divisions are stated.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x4C3790..0x4C394A; the global's only writer is 0xCB593B in the initialiser at 0xCB5920 (`movss xmm0,[0x160a688]` = 250.5f, floor, _ftol2). A whole-.text scan for 0x1A8732C finds that writer and the one read at 0x4C38FA.

addresses.name: CAlignment::GetProximityTerm
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall CAlignment::GetProximityTerm(int* out, CIdeologyGroup* group, CCountry* country)
addresses.comment: Zero unless the country is unaligned and the group's faction has members. For each member m: d = CMap::DistanceBetweenProvinces between the two **acting** capitals (+0xE24) - isqrt(16 x (dx^2 + dy^2)) on the provinces' **bounding-box centres** (CProvinceTemplate +0x2C/+0x30), x wrapped at half the map width, so four times the pixel distance; t = (5000000 - 1000 x d) x 1000 / 500000, i.e. 10 - d/500 in thousandths, **floored at 100** (0.1, [0x1A87334], floor(100.5f) from InitAlignmentProximityFloor); r = m.maxIC / country.maxIC (CCountry +0x60C, whole IC, **integer** divide; r = m.maxIC undivided when the country's is 0, which the base_values IC of 5 makes unreachable); v = r x 1000 x t / 1000. best = the largest v, starting from 0. Then best x PROXIMITY_WEIGHT (alignment +0xC) / 1000 x (1000 + SUSEPTIBILITY) / 1000 x (1000 + suseptibility_<faction>) / 1000. A member no larger than the country gives nothing; a country with five IC beside Germany's 144 gets 28 times the distance factor.
addresses.revises: The floor global is now known (100, i.e. 0.1); the distance's unit and the point it is measured between are stated, and the integer arithmetic is written out.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x4C3C00..0x4C3E3D; the global's only writer is 0xCB587B (100.5f at 0x160A684). The start save is the check: with the bounding-box centres 93 of 101 countries' day-one moves agree to the thousandth, with positions.txt's unit points put over them 54 - Berlin's unit point is y 1729 and its box centre 1728. So the distance is measured between box centres and positions.txt does not move them (measured, FINDINGS-alignment.md section 4).

addresses.name: LeaThisPlusE4
addresses.comment: `lea eax,[ecx+0xe4]; ret`. A compiler fold, recorded class-free per trap 4: luabind registers it as CCountry::GetAlignmentCord (the Lua half's CCountry +0xE4 `AlignmentCord`, the alignment position) **and** as CAIStrategy::GetTheatres, and it sits in CGraphicalTableLedger slot 47. CAlignmentPosition::Apply calls it on the country to keep the old position.
addresses.evidence: Two instructions. vtable.py --holding: CGraphicalTableLedger slot 47; ghidra/luabind.json: two accessor registrations at 004F6CD0. Its one direct caller is 0x5F0BB7.

addresses.name: CCountry::SetAlignmentCord
addresses.comment: `country->alignment.position = *position` - +0xE4 and +0xE8 (CAlignment +0x8/+0xC) copied from the point in eax, **no clamp**. Named after the game's own getter, CCountry::GetAlignmentCord. Its only callers are the two arms of CAlignmentPosition::Apply (0x5F0BD7, 0x5F0BEA), so it is how a history `alignment = { x y }` reaches the country.
addresses.evidence: Five instructions, bare `ret` at 0x4F6CF1; in no virtual table and not in luabind.json. findRefs --callers gives the two sites.

addresses.name: CAlignmentPosition::CAlignmentPosition
addresses.comment: CCountryHistoryEntry::CCountryHistoryEntry(country), vftable 0x15C99C4, then the two points at +0x10 (the position the history gives) and +0x18 (the one it replaced) zeroed. `ret 4`. One caller, CCountryHistory::LoadEntry's `alignment` case (0x5ED64C), which allocates 0x20 bytes, reads the block with ParsePoint (0xA7B8D0) and hands it to SetPosition.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x5F0B40..0x5F0B7A; findRefs --vftable CAlignmentPosition finds the one store at 0x5F0B58; operator new(0x20) at 0x5ED617.

addresses.name: CAlignmentPosition::SetPosition
addresses.comment: Copies the point into +0x10 (0x418980, a two-dword copy). `ret 4`. Called once, by the history loader after ParsePoint.
addresses.evidence: Seven instructions; the call at 0x5ED693 follows ParsePoint at 0x5ED687 on the same local.

addresses.name: CAlignmentPosition::Apply
addresses.comment: Slot 7, `alignment = { x y }` in a country's history. Forward: keeps the country's current position (LeaThisPlusE4) at +0x18, then CCountry::SetAlignmentCord(country, +0x10); backward: SetAlignmentCord(country, the kept +0x18). **Nothing clamps it** - a history point outside the triangle stays outside until the first drift step. `ret 4`, 0x5F0BA0..0x5F0BF2.
addresses.evidence: Decoded in full; vtable.py --holding: CAlignmentPosition slot 7 only. Same shape as CNeutralityChange::Apply and CThreatChange::Apply.

addresses.name: CAlignmentPosition::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2: writes the point at +0x10 under token 0x6BC, `alignment`, through the point writer 0xA7A080. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Nine instructions; vtable.py --holding: CAlignmentPosition slot 2 only. The token agrees with GetSaveToken.

addresses.name: CAlignmentPosition::GetSaveToken
addresses.comment: Slot 6: `mov eax, 0x6bc; ret` in a frame - the `alignment` token. The bodies beside it answer 0x6BD and 0x4FB for their own classes.
addresses.evidence: Decoded; vtable.py --holding: CAlignmentPosition slot 6 only, so not a fold.

addresses.name: CCgmAlignmentChangeCommand::Execute
addresses.comment: Slot 6. The custom game's alignment change: countries[this->+0x40]->alignment.position = (this->+0x60, this->+0x64), then CAlignment::ClampPosition, then the in-game screen's diplomacy refresh for the tag at +0x3C. Outside the canonical start. Bare `ret` at 0x429C48.
addresses.evidence: Decoded; vtable.py --holding: CCgmAlignmentChangeCommand slot 6 only, the slot CCgmNeutralityChangeCommand::Execute holds in its own table.

addresses.name: InitAlignmentProximityFloor
addresses.comment: A C runtime initialiser: floor(100.5f) (the float at 0x160A684, via 0x401FD0 and _ftol2_sse) into g_AlignmentProximityFloor - **100, the fixed-point 0.1**. Not a define (trap 8, the third way).
addresses.evidence: Seven instructions, 0xCB5860..0xCB5880; the float reads 100.5 as f32. The same shape as InitFixedPoint0_100 (rva 0x8B0FA0), which floors the same float into a different global.

addresses.name: InitAlignmentInfluenceFloor
addresses.comment: A C runtime initialiser: floor(250.5f) (the float at 0x160A688) into g_AlignmentInfluenceFloor - **250, the fixed-point 0.25**. Not a define.
addresses.evidence: Seven instructions, 0xCB5920..0xCB5940; the float reads 250.5 as f32.

addresses.name: g_AlignmentProximityFloor
addresses.no_signature: A global int, not a function.
addresses.comment: 100 (0.1) once the runtime has started: the floor on the proximity term's distance factor 10 - d/500, so a faction member any distance away still counts a tenth. Written only by InitAlignmentProximityFloor; read only by CAlignment::GetProximityTerm (0x4C3D17).
addresses.evidence: findRefs --address 0x1A87334: two references in .text, the initialiser's store at 0xCB587B and the read at 0x4C3D17. It lies in .bss, which is why no static value could be read.

addresses.name: g_AlignmentInfluenceFloor
addresses.no_signature: A global int, not a function.
addresses.comment: 250 (0.25) once the runtime has started: added to the country's (1 - neutrality/100) in the influence term and also its floor. Written only by InitAlignmentInfluenceFloor; read only by CAlignment::GetAlignTowardsTerm (0x4C38FA).
addresses.evidence: findRefs --address 0x1A8732C: two references, the store at 0xCB593B and the read at 0x4C38FA.

structs.name: CAlignmentPosition
structs.comment: `alignment = { x y }` in a country's history: a CCountryHistoryEntry (country at +0xC) carrying the position to set (+0x10) and the one it replaced (+0x18). Applied without a clamp.
structs.evidence: The loader allocates 0x20 bytes (0x5ED617) and runs the constructor 0x5F0B40, which calls CCountryHistoryEntry's constructor and writes vftable 0x15C99C4; the RTTI export gives CCountryHistoryEntry as its one base at offset 0.

struct_fields.name: position_x
struct_fields.comment: The x the history gives, thousandths (ParsePoint).
struct_fields.evidence: SetPosition copies into +0x10; Apply passes this + 0x10 to SetAlignmentCord; SaveContents writes it.

struct_fields.name: position_y
struct_fields.comment: The y the history gives, thousandths.
struct_fields.evidence: The second dword of the point at +0x10.

struct_fields.name: previous_x
struct_fields.comment: The country's position before Apply forward, put back by Apply backward.
struct_fields.evidence: Apply forward copies LeaThisPlusE4(country) into this + 0x18; backward passes this + 0x18 to SetAlignmentCord.

struct_fields.name: previous_y
struct_fields.evidence: The second dword of the point at +0x18.

struct_fields.name: centroid_x
struct_fields.comment: The centroid of the bounds triangle, x, thousandths - written by CAlignment::UpdateCentroid after every clamp. No reader found.
struct_fields.evidence: UpdateCentroid's store at 0x4C4983; the constructor zeroes it.

struct_fields.name: centroid_y
struct_fields.comment: The centroid's y, minY + 2/3 of the height (84.667 in Their Finest Hour). No reader found.

struct_fields.name: bounds_min_y
struct_fields.comment: The bounds box's least y, thousandths; the box starts at (0, 0) with no size and grows to every group's position, so it always holds the origin.
struct_fields.evidence: RebuildBounds' minimum-y arm; ClampMove's y floor and ClampPosition's.

struct_fields.name: bounds_width
struct_fields.comment: The box's width; RebuildBounds runs only while this and the height are both 0.
struct_fields.evidence: RebuildBounds' entry test at 0x4C46D0..; minX + width is ClampMove's x ceiling.

struct_fields.name: bounds_height
struct_fields.comment: The box's height; minY + height is the y ceiling and the triangle's top.
struct_fields.evidence: RebuildBounds' maximum-y arm; ClampMove's y ceiling.

struct_fields.name: right_edge_slope
struct_fields.comment: -height x 1000 / (mid - maxX): the right edge's slope from the apex at the bottom middle, +1730 in Their Finest Hour. A point's right limit at height y is (y - apexY) x 1000 / this, measured from x 0.
struct_fields.evidence: RebuildBounds' store; ClampMove divides (y - [+0x40]) x 1000 by it for the right limit.

struct_fields.name: left_edge_slope
struct_fields.comment: -height x 1000 / (mid - minX), -1730 in Their Finest Hour; the left limit is (y - apexY) x 1000 / this.
struct_fields.evidence: RebuildBounds' store; ClampMove divides (y - [+0x44]) x 1000 by it for the left limit.

struct_fields.name: apex_y_right
struct_fields.comment: The triangle's apex y (= minY), the base the right limit is measured from.
struct_fields.evidence: RebuildBounds stores minY to +0x40 and +0x44; ClampMove subtracts +0x40 before dividing by +0x38.

struct_fields.name: apex_y_left
struct_fields.comment: The same apex y, the base the left limit is measured from.

struct_fields.name: next_alignment_update
struct_fields.comment: A tick, **not saved and not loaded** (neither CCountry::LoadKey nor SaveContents touches it), set to the null date [0x170C2B8] = 43800000 (year 0) by the constructor and CCountry_Reset. The daily pass runs CAlignment::UpdateDaily only when today > this, then sets it to today + (ALIGNMENT_INTERVAL / 1000) x 24. So the first daily pass after a new game **or a load** drifts every unaligned country at once, and because the test is strict and the day's tick is its hour 0, **a step comes every ALIGNMENT_INTERVAL + 1 days** - 25 in Their Finest Hour and BlackICE, which both set 24. A new game's first step is its first day, before the first hour (Jan 1, then Jan 26, Feb 20, Mar 17, Apr 11).
struct_fields.revises: The record said the step is every 24 days and said nothing of saving. It is not saved (so a load resets the schedule), the null date makes day one a step, and the strict `>` makes the period 25 days.
struct_fields.evidence: The sweep of every store to +0x124 in .text finds CCountry::CCountry 0x4C8BBD and CCountry_Reset 0x4D3214 (both [0x170C2B8]) and the daily pass 0x4DB8FA/0x4DB925; none in LoadKey (0x4CCDA0..) or SaveContents, where the same sweep finds +0x98 and +0xA8C (positive control). The gate is `cmp eax,[ebx+0x124]; jle skip` at 0x4DB86A. The saves agree: all eight January saves of the 9 October game hold the start positions, and Jan 8 -> Feb 1, Feb 1 -> Mar 1 and Apr 1 -> Apr 20 each fit one step.

slots_noted: LeaThisPlusE4 (rva 0xF6CD0) is a fold - CGraphicalTableLedger slot 47 and two luabind registrations - and is recorded class-free, so no slot record is offered for it.
